outcomes: A Go or TypeScript caller switches on the same four outcomes and retries only a serialization failure
Every database adapter runs the same ordered scenario corpus and must reach the same outcome in each scenario
A result serializes to the same bytes in every language
nonGoals: Running a unit of work: the framework database adapters run it and own WithTx and runInTransaction
Savepoint-scoped nesting: nested joins the enclosing transaction, and a savepoint mode would be a new value and a protocol version bump
Executing the corpus against a live PostgreSQL: the adapters' conformance runners do it when a test database is bound

requirements.text: A unit of work and a result parse strictly. An unknown member, a protocolVersion other than 1, a missing propagation or outcome, a value outside a closed set, an invalid name, and a retryable member that contradicts the outcome are refused. Every valid fixture parses clean, every invalid one is refused, and every code the validators emit is registered.

Of the four outcomes applied, already-consumed-conflict, not-found and retryable-serialization-failure, only retryable-serialization-failure is retryable; every other outcome is terminal. The TypeScript adapter of @putnami/database exposes exactly these four values and treats only the same one as retryable.

A result serializes to the same bytes on every marshal, and those bytes equal the committed equivalence golden that another language must reproduce. Re-serializing a parsed valid fixture yields the same bytes again.

The unit-of-work and result schemas carry exactly the members of the Go types, require propagation, outcome and protocolVersion as the Go validators do, pin protocolVersion to the Go constant, and list the same closed enums as the Go types.

conformance/manifest.json is the one ordered scenario corpus of the database adapters. It validates strictly, holds the six required scenarios, and the embedded copy equals the file. Its fixtures get their verdict, each reject branch has a fixture with its own code, and its schema lists the Go enums. @putnami/database ships a byte-identical copy of it.

conformance/pack.json gives the corpus the stable id putnami.transaction.conformance, the languages go and typescript, a corpus pointer that resolves to the embedded corpus, and capability kinds that the capabilities protocol defines.

The Go database adapter answers with these outcomes. Compare-and-set, consume-once and rotate return applied, already-consumed-conflict or not-found, a serialization failure or a deadlock is the retryable outcome, a unique violation is a conflict, and a genuine I/O error stays an error. A rotation inserts no successor for a predecessor already rotated.

The TypeScript adapter of @putnami/database classifies a Postgres error by its SQLSTATE: 40001 and 40P01 are retryable-serialization-failure, 23505 is already-consumed-conflict, and any other code, an error that does not come from Postgres and an absent error stay unclassified.
